title: Menstrual health and reusable pad skills
source_title: Community based awareness and capacity building on Menstrual Health Management (MHM) and skill training for Vulnerable Adolescent Girls and Young Women (AGYW) affected by armed conflict.
excerpt: A Women2030 proposal combining menstrual health education, action against stigma and reusable sanitary pad skills for adolescent girls and young women affected by armed conflict in Bamenda.
overview: The application responds to menstrual health challenges experienced by internally displaced adolescent girls and young women in crowded host households. It proposes combining community education with practical skills that support personal menstrual care and potential income generation.
objectives: Improve understanding of menstrual health management and challenge stigma and gender inequality.
Equip vulnerable adolescent girls and young women with skills to produce reusable sanitary pads.
Build the capacity of teachers, parents and community leaders to promote supportive menstrual health practices.
activities: Stakeholder consultations and selection of participants and trainers.
A one-day workshop for a proposed 40 participants: 20 community members and 20 adolescent girls and young women.
Two months of reusable pad production training for 20 adolescent girls and young women, with monitoring and review meetings.
evidence_notes: Funding application to Women2030. Participant numbers and benefits are proposed targets; this document does not establish completion or grant approval.

title: Safe spaces for girls’ health and advocacy
source_title: Creating Safe Spaces for AGYW Living with or at Risk of HIV to Access Better SRH Services and Advocate for their SRHR.
excerpt: A HER Voice Fund application for HIV and sexual and reproductive health education, research on service barriers, an ambassadors forum and advocacy led by adolescent girls and young women in Yaoundé III.
overview: The project proposes a supportive environment in which adolescent girls and young women aged 14–24 can learn about HIV and sexual and reproductive health and rights, discuss their experiences and develop confidence to advocate for better services and policies.
objectives: Provide HIV, sexual and reproductive health and policy education to a proposed 100 adolescent girls and young women.
Investigate service barriers through research targeting 300 adolescent girls and young women.
Create safe spaces for public speaking, peer support and policy advocacy.
activities: Stakeholder launch and education workshops adapted to COVID-19 gathering restrictions.
Research using questionnaires, focus groups and key informant interviews.
An ambassadors forum, radio dialogues and engagement with national HIV and Global Fund processes.
evidence_notes: The application describes intended activities. The separate September 2020 research report documents the research component and is catalogued independently; it does not prove completion of every proposed activity.

title: Understanding barriers to HIV and reproductive health services
source_title: Research on barriers faced by adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) in accessing HIV and sexual and reproductive health services
location: Yaoundé III Municipality and surrounding neighbourhoods, Cameroon
excerpt: A September 2020 research report examining the knowledge, cost, stigma, confidentiality and service access barriers experienced by adolescent girls and young women aged 14–24 in Yaoundé III.
overview: HOVUCA’s research examines how adolescent girls and young women experience HIV and sexual and reproductive health services. The report acknowledges Y+Global support through the HER Voice Fund and combines survey responses with stakeholder interviews and young people’s discussions.
objectives: Document barriers to availability, accessibility and affordability of HIV and sexual and reproductive health services.
Understand young women’s knowledge, service experiences and policy-related concerns.
Use the findings to inform advocacy for more accessible and respectful services.
activities: The report records 302 quantitative survey participants, eight key informant interviews and four focus group discussions.
Analysis of awareness, stigma, confidentiality, service costs and human rights concerns.
findings: The report identifies fear of judgement, confidentiality concerns, costs, transport and service opening hours as access barriers.
Recommendations include comprehensive education, clearer information on where services are available and youth-friendly care that respects privacy and informed consent.
evidence_notes: Completed research is documented in the supplied report. These are historical study findings, not current prevalence estimates or evidence that the broader safe-spaces project achieved every intended outcome.

title: Girls’ participation in HIV policy and advocacy
source_title: A Policy analysis and advocacy project to engage AGYW in National HIV programmes and Global Fund Processes
location: Cameroon; location not specified in the implementation plan
reporting_period: 2021 archive; schedule runs June–March without explicit calendar years
excerpt: An implementation plan for policy analysis, leadership development, school HIV clubs and participation by adolescent girls and young women in national HIV programmes and Global Fund processes.
overview: The plan sets out a pathway for adolescent girls and young women to study HIV policies, identify gaps and speak directly to decision makers. It links policy analysis with practical leadership and public speaking skills.
objectives: Enable adolescent girls and young women to review national HIV policy and advocate for reforms.
Build leadership, confidence and public speaking skills among in-school and out-of-school participants.
Support participation in HIV planning meetings and Global Fund processes.
activities: An advocacy speech-writing competition and a briefing with policy makers.
Continuation of an ambassadors forum and HIV clubs in three schools.
A press conference, advocacy for accessible testing and treatment, monitoring and reporting.
evidence_notes: Implementation plan, not a completion report. The archive folder supplies the year; the document’s month-only schedule does not establish exact start or end dates.

title: School health education and economic empowerment
excerpt: A HER Voice Fund proposal to expand comprehensive sexuality education in Yaoundé schools, strengthen girls’ participation in HIV decision making and support economic skills for vulnerable young women.
overview: The proposal builds on earlier school education and advocacy work. It combines comprehensive sexuality education, HIV and gender-based violence prevention with support for adolescent girls and young women to participate in policy spaces and develop greater economic self-reliance.
objectives: Advocate for comprehensive sexuality education in education policies and school curricula.
Reach a proposed 1,600 adolescent girls in Yaoundé with health education by December 2022.
Support participation in HIV programmes and Global Fund processes and provide business skills to vulnerable young women, including those living with HIV.
activities: Stakeholder mobilisation and launch meetings.
School education, policy review and advocacy briefs.
Participation in HIV technical working groups and other decision-making platforms, alongside economic skills training.
evidence_notes: Application with proposed targets and indicators. No completion report is supplied for this annual project; no achieved participant count is inferred.

title: Road show activation for pneumonia
location: Peri-urban and rural areas of Mfou District, Cameroon
reporting_period: World Pneumonia Day, 12 November 2022, proposed event
excerpt: A World Pneumonia Day small-grant proposal for a community road show in Mfou District, promoting recognition of childhood pneumonia, challenging myths and bringing children’s voices into health awareness.
overview: The proposal uses a public road show to bring pneumonia awareness to peri-urban and rural communities. Its focus is the health of children under five and the role of families and community members in recognising illness and seeking support.
objectives: Mobilise a proposed 2,000 community members around childhood pneumonia awareness.
Share knowledge on signs and symptoms and challenge misconceptions.
Promote children’s participation and voices in matters affecting their health.
activities: Community mobilisation and a road show activation linked to World Pneumonia Day.
Public education and messages on childhood pneumonia.
evidence_notes: Small-grant application. The audience size and event date are proposed; the document does not confirm the event occurred or the grant was awarded.

title: Girls’ leadership and reproductive rights advocacy
excerpt: A HER Voice Fund proposal for communication and leadership skills, school health education, policy review and community advocacy against harmful norms that restrict girls’ reproductive health and rights.
overview: The proposal places adolescent girls and young women at the centre of advocacy for sexual and reproductive health and rights. It addresses gender-based violence, harmful cultural practices and policy barriers through school education, multimedia advocacy and engagement with decision makers.
objectives: Strengthen communication and leadership in reproductive rights advocacy.
Mobilise communities against harmful norms and support participation in HIV policy processes.
Support girls and young women to identify legal and policy barriers to accessible services.
activities: A stakeholder launch, desk review and advocacy briefing with legal and policy stakeholders.
A community advocacy run to challenge harmful cultural practices.
Health and rights education in five schools targeting over 2,000 adolescent girls, multimedia advocacy and participation in a national AGYW summit.
evidence_notes: Annual funding application. School reach and intended reductions in HIV and gender-based violence are targets, not verified results.

title: Strengthening sexuality education in schools
source_title: Reduction of the incidence of HIV amongst adolescent girls in schools through improve communication and leadership skills of adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) in Sexual and Reproductive Health and advocacy in the Mfoundi Division
location: Yaoundé III, VI and VII; training in Mbalmayo, Cameroon
excerpt: A request to UNFPA to strengthen HER Voice school activities through stakeholder consultation, peer educator training, longer sexuality education programmes and teacher capacity building.
overview: The request seeks additional support for school-based sexuality education aligned with the Education Plus initiative. It proposes extending lessons from eight to sixteen sessions and building continuity through trained teachers and peer educators.
objectives: Engage decision makers on integrating sexuality education into school curricula.
Train a proposed 24 adolescent girls and young women as peer educators and advocates.
Reach a proposed 2,000 adolescent girls in eight schools and train 24 teachers.
activities: A consultation with policy makers and education stakeholders.
A two-day peer educator workshop in Mbalmayo.
Peer-led lessons in Yaoundé schools and teacher training to sustain the programme.
evidence_notes: Request for support. The 2024 CFLI application separately describes earlier UNFPA-supported outputs, but its school counts differ from this proposal’s targets. This record preserves the proposal scope without converting targets into results.

title: Youth health education in schools and communities
source_title: Reduction in the rate of HIV, drug use and teenage pregnancies amongst adolescents and youths in and out of school in Yaounde through knowledge sharing on comprehensive sexuality education in schools and community
location: Biyem-Assi and Efoulan districts, Yaoundé, Cameroon
sources: 2024/CFLI FINAL PROJECT APPLICATION FOR FUNDING FORM HOVUCA..docx
excerpt: A Canada Fund for Local Initiatives application combining peer-led school and community education with teacher training, boys’ advocacy and parent engagement around young people’s health and rights.
overview: The application proposes sexuality education in schools and community settings to address HIV, drug use and teenage pregnancy among adolescents and young people. It includes girls and boys, in-school and out-of-school participants, and adults who influence their access to information.
objectives: Build young people’s knowledge and ability to make informed health decisions.
Train a proposed 20 peer educators and 20 teachers.
Deliver education to a proposed 2,400 pupils in five schools and 100 young people in five community areas.
activities: Stakeholder consultation and peer education training.
School lessons and outreach to vulnerable and displaced young people, including proposed dignity kit distribution.
Teacher capacity building, boys’ advocacy and parent and community leader engagement.
evidence_notes: Funding application. Project dates are explicitly July 2024–January 2025, but the goal refers to February 2025 and the signature shows May 2025; these inconsistencies require organizational confirmation. The listed activity targets are not completion evidence.

title: Amplifying girls’ voices in Tonga
source_title: Empowering and Amplifying AGYW Voices: Advocating for CSE, SRHR, TB and Malaria Access and Rights for Adolescent Girls and Young Women (AGYW) in Tonga, West Region of Cameroon
excerpt: A multi-year HER Voice Fund proposal for resident and displaced girls and young women in Tonga, combining baseline research, health education, community engagement and participation in health decision making.
overview: The proposal responds to the health and rights needs of adolescent girls and young women in Tonga, including those displaced by conflict. It links education and advocacy on sexual and reproductive health, HIV, tuberculosis and malaria with engagement of parents, teachers, health workers and community leaders.
objectives: Create opportunities to share health information with a proposed 1,500 adolescent girls and young women by September 2026.
Support participation in district health and gender-based violence platforms.
Challenge harmful norms and advocate for more accessible, affordable services.
activities: Community consultations, project launch and baseline research.
Peer-led comprehensive sexuality education and engagement of men, boys and community stakeholders.
Support for girls’ participation in decision-making forums and public awareness advocacy.
evidence_notes: Multi-year application. A December 2024 baseline report is supplied and catalogued separately. It documents a research component; the wider project’s current delivery status and final outcomes remain unverified.

title: Mapping girls’ access to health services in Tonga
source_title: Baseline research on the Provision of comprehensive sexuality education and sexual and reproductive health, Tuberculosis and Malaria services for adolescents and young women in Tonga, Cameroon
location: 20 quarters in Tonga District, West Region, Cameroon
sources: Docs to publish/Report of the Baseline Research in Tonga 2024 -HOVUCA.docx
2024/Report of the Baseline Research in Tonga 2024 -HOVUCA.docx
excerpt: A mixed-methods baseline study of health knowledge, access and service quality for resident and displaced girls and young women aged 15–29 across Tonga District, supporting evidence-led HER Voice programming.
overview: The report establishes a baseline for HOVUCA and Y+Global’s HER Voice work in Tonga. It examines sexuality education and sexual and reproductive health, HIV, tuberculosis and malaria services, alongside gender norms, violence and participation in decision-making spaces.
objectives: Assess knowledge, attitudes and service access among resident and internally displaced adolescent girls and young women.
Identify gaps in service availability, accessibility and quality.
Inform targeted advocacy and programme design.
activities: The report records surveys of 600 adolescent girls and young women and interviews with 18 key stakeholders across 20 quarters.
A cross-sectional mixed-methods assessment with informed consent and confidentiality procedures.
findings: The report identifies gaps in sexuality education, menstrual health knowledge and awareness of pregnancy prevention methods.
Stigma, limited information and social norms affect access to health services.
The recommendations call for stronger education, youth-friendly services and community engagement.
evidence_notes: Two supplied copies describe the same study and are merged into one record. A baseline measures starting conditions; it does not demonstrate changes caused by the multi-year project. Findings are historical and specific to the sampled population.

title: Peer-led sexuality education in Yaoundé schools
source_title: Impact Knowledge on Comprehensive Sexuality Education (CSE) to Adolescent Girls in schools in Yaounde
location: Yaoundé III, VI and VII; training in Mbalmayo, Cameroon
reporting_period: 2024 activities; July training and October–November school sessions proposed
excerpt: A request to UNAIDS for peer educator training and weekly sexuality education sessions for a proposed 750 adolescent girls in five additional Yaoundé schools.
overview: The request seeks to extend HOVUCA’s school education work to institutions identified as lacking comprehensive sexuality education. Young women would lead lessons during school club hours or free periods.
objectives: Train a proposed 16 adolescent girls and young women in sexuality education and peer leadership.
Provide a proposed 750 schoolgirls with sexuality education across five schools.
Support informed decisions about sexual and reproductive health and rights.
activities: A two-day peer educator workshop in Mbalmayo.
Agreement with school authorities on appropriate teaching periods.
Weekly peer-led education for eight weeks, followed by monitoring and reporting.
evidence_notes: Request for support, not a completion report. The document contains an older August 2023–March 2024 schedule heading alongside 2024 activity dates; exact implementation dates require confirmation.

title: Youth health education in Bamenda and Garoua
source_title: Comprehensive Sexuality Education (CSE) to improve the Sexual and Reproductive Health of Conflict Affected Adolescents and Youths in the Peri-Urban Areas of Bamenda and in Garoua during University games.
excerpt: A UNFPA proposal for sexuality education and youth-friendly health information in conflict-affected Bamenda, alongside peer education and awareness activities at the university games in Garoua.
overview: The proposal combines school-based education with a structured peer network for out-of-school and conflict-affected young people. A separate strand supports education and health service awareness at the university games in Garoua.
objectives: Train a proposed 30 peer educators in Bamenda and reach 2,000 pupils and 500 out-of-school young people.
Assess the provision of sexuality education and adolescent health services in Bamenda.
Train a proposed 50 university games peer educators, support awareness for 10,000 young people and service access for 300.
activities: Stakeholder consultation, peer educator training and school lessons.
A peer educator–peer promoter–peer contact network for community education.
A rapid survey and validation workshop, plus training and awareness activities in Garoua.
evidence_notes: Proposal submitted to UNFPA. All reach figures are proposed targets. Exact calendar days and achieved outcomes are not established by this document.
